title: HarborPay runtime error scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Customer: HarborPay (private deployment, VPC). Reported intermittent 5xxs and duplicated tokens in generated output for payments reconciliation path. Deployment: v1.3.2 (runtime build 2026-02-18). Model pinned: rw-inference-m-7b-q4 (quantized).

What I saw (high level):
- Multiple user reports between 2026-03-07 02:15-03:40 UTC of failed reconciliation jobs (batch size 1).
- Platform alerts: route horus-payments-01 crossing error rate threshold at ~02:12 UTC, auto-fallback triggered to smaller model variant at 02:14 but fallback also returned 500 for a window.

Commands / Queries I ran (notes + outputs):
1) kubectl logs -n harbor-pay deployments/rw-runtime -c runtime --tail=200\- 02:13:44 UTC repeated: "ERROR: Runtime inference loop: AssertionError: kv cache size mismatch (expected 2048, got 1920)"
2) kubectl get pods -n harbor-pay -o wide\- pod rw-runtime-5ff8c Ready 1/2 (restarts=3) node=gpu-2
3) kubectl describe pod rw-runtime-5ff8c -n harbor-pay\- Events: OOMKilled at 02:11 then restart; readiness probe failed 5x; liveness probe restart 2x
4) curl -s -D - http://10.8.4.22:8080/health | sed -n '1,20p'\- HTTP/1.1 200 OK (when pod healthy) or 503 Service Unavailable (during incident window)
5) tail -n 500 /var/log/rw/runtime.log | grep -E "KV|cache|OOM|cuda"\- sample entries:
   [2026-03-07T02:11:20Z] WARN  KVCache: evicting stale prefix 0..128
   [2026-03-07T02:11:21Z] ERROR RuntimeHandlers: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory (CUDA error 2)
   [2026-03-07T02:12:05Z] ERROR Runtime: AssertionError: kv cache segment mismatch at token_step=24 expected_offset=2048 actual=1920
6) gcloud compute ssh gpu-2 -- tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog\- kernel logs showing page allocation failure around 02:11:19 UTC (suspect memory pressure)

Sample request/response snippet captured from customer logs (redacted):
- request-id: rp_3f2a
- input: "reconcile_batch: txn_ids=[...]")
- runtime error: {"error":"internal_error","message":"AssertionError: kv cache size mismatch (expected 2048, got 1920)"}

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kv-cache / continuous-batching edgecase: quantized model + long prefix + batching caused inconsistent KV offsets after OOM/restart during concurrent requests. Root cause likely bug that doesn't reset cache pointers on partial eviction.
2) Memory fragmentation / driver interaction: GPU OOM triggered partial allocations, subsequent memcpy used stale pointer leading to mismatch.
3) Deployment config: autoscaler allowed multiple warm containers with different cache segment sizing (rare but possible with mixed kernel flags).
4) Customer workload: they sent very long sequences (avg seq_len 6k for some reconciliation payloads) which exacerbated kv size and OOM risk.

Quick repro notes (local-ish):
- Repro attempt on dev-gpu: run quantized model with prefix length 6k and two concurrent streams with continuous batching enabled. Observed similar assertion after ~15-20 minutes with mem pressure. Commands:
  docker run --gpus all --env RW_MODE=serve rw/runtime:dev2026-02 bash -c "python tools/run_repro.py --prefix-len 6000 --concurrency 2 --quantize q4"
- logs show same AssertionError after OOM sequence.

Mitigations applied during outage:
- 02:14:10 UTC: automated fallback to smaller model variant (rw-inference-m-3b-q4) — reduced error rate but some 500s persisted while pods restarted.
- 02:18:00 UTC: scaled down batch size to 1 and disabled continuous-batching at route via console (temp).
- 02:22:30 UTC: applied pod annotation to disable kernel-optimizations=experimental on gpu-2 (worked around weird memcpy behavior)

Customer-facing draft (short) — DO NOT SEND yet (internal draft):
"Hi HarborPay team,

We’re investigating the intermittent 5xx errors you saw early Saturday. Initial findings point to a runtime memory-handling issue triggered by very long reconciliation payloads combined with a quantized model and continuous batching. We applied a temporary mitigations (reduced batch size, disabled continuous batching, fallback to smaller model) which have stopped the errors for now.

Next steps: we will deploy a targeted runtime patch to fix the kv cache reset behavior and run extended soak tests against your workload. We expect a stable fix and verification within 72 hours. I’ll follow up with more details and a timeline tomorrow.

Apologies for the disruption — Ethan (oncall)
"

Internal comms draft for eng-runtime (bullet):
- Incident INC-4921: kv-cache mismatch + GPU OOM on harbor-pay private deployment
- Root cause hypothesis: cache pointer not reset after partial eviction / OOM during continuous batching with quantized model
- Repro: local repro using tools/run_repro.py with prefix-len 6000 + concurrency 2 (see linked PR for quick patch)
- Immediate action: backport runtime patch that performs explicit KVCache::reset() during allocation failure path + extended soak (24h) on staging with customer traces
- Owner: Priya (lead runtime), Lina (oncall infra), Ethan (CS liaison)

Next steps / TODO (personal):
- [ ] Push hotfix branch to staging (PR created: review + run CI) — PR: linked_artifacts[2]
- [ ] Coordinate with HarborPay infra to run soak tests overnight (ask for 2x replay of typical workload)
- [ ] Add special-case metric: kv_cache_mismatch_count and GPU_page_alloc_failures to console alerting (SLO review)
- [ ] Draft postmortem outline in Confluence (assign sections)

Notes to self / friction points:
- Need a better local repro harness that reproduces memory fragmentation behavior w/o full customer data — tools/run_repro.py is close but needs tuning for timing and allocation patterns.
- Consider adding guard rails to autoscaler to avoid heterogeneous kernel flags on same nodepool.

Attachments / logs I saved to incident folder:
- /incidents/INC-4921/runtime-rw-runtime-5ff8c.log (snippet saved)
- flamegraph from 02:10-02:25 attached (will upload to confluence)

Timestamped timeline (rough):
- 02:10:43 UTC: first alert - route error rate spike
- 02:11:19 UTC: kernel page alloc failure on gpu-2 (syslog) -> OOM kill of runtime container
- 02:11:21 UTC: first AssertionError: kv cache segment mismatch logged
- 02:12:05 UTC: multiple 500s observed, automated fallback triggered at 02:14
- 02:18:00 UTC: manual mitigation applied (disable continuous-batching, batch_size=1)
- 02:22:30 UTC: experimental kernel-optimizations disabled -> error rate drops

If anything new appears I will append here. Will follow up after hotfix CI results.

Ethan
